note: The ONLY hand-written input to data/art-register.json. Everything else in that file is derived by scripts/build-art-register.py; this holds the claims no machine in this repo can make. Read by that script, validated harshly, and the loader REFUSES the whole file rather than skipping a bad entry -- a skipped entry resurfaces as a fresh 'unknown' and sends the next person hunting a bug nobody introduced.
the_rule: An entry here is an assertion about the world, so it carries a clock. verify=human costs why_not_machine plus a human_verified stamp with a review_by that EXPIRES; past that date scripts/check-art-staleness.py is RED on 'this verification expired', never on the underlying image. Same shape as content/campaigns/README.md section 2.1 and scripts/acknowledgements.py. Do not add an entry you would not re-check on the review date.
what_does_NOT_belong_here: A guess. If nothing in this repo and nobody's actual knowledge supports the claim, leave the file out and let the register say origin=unknown. Unknown is a first-class value and today it is the commonest one; that is the honest state, not a gap to be filled in.

origin: generated -- a model produced the pixels
photograph -- a camera captured a real subject (further processing does not change this)
human-illustrated -- a person drew or painted it
screenshot -- a capture of the game's own rendered UI
unknown -- nothing here records which of the above it is
vocabulary.verify: checked | delegated | online | human | durable -- copied from content/campaigns/README.md section 2.1. Do not invent a sixth tier.

assertions.why_not_machine: The claim is that a real camera photographed a real cat. The only in-repo evidence is prose on the page that displays the image plus a comment in deploy-excludes.txt, and matching a gallery file to its original in assets/dump/ needs fuzzy name matching ('web-arwen.jpg' vs 'arwen matilda.jpeg'). A regex over page prose is exactly the pattern-matching that gave check-platform-claims.py two false positives; a human reading two sentences is more reliable and says so.

deliberately_absent.assets/cats-gallery/web-doom-cat.jpg: The eighth image in the same gallery, and it stays UNKNOWN on purpose. Its alt text calls it 'The original AI Safety guardian' rather than naming a custodian, and the nearest file in assets/dump/ is 'zoomed in doom cat.png' -- a PNG among the custodians' JPEGs. Asserting 'photograph' for it because its seven neighbours are photographs is the generalisation this repo has been bitten by twice (the retired-mirror bullet in CLAUDE.md, and the _deprecated note on game-changes.json). Seven of eight is the honest answer.
deliberately_absent.assets/screenshots/*: Almost certainly captures of the game's own UI, but 'almost certainly' is a guess and the register is not the place for one. optimize-screenshots.py proves the -web variants DERIVE from the .png masters; it says nothing about where a master came from.
deliberately_absent.assets/pdoom_logo_1.png: scripts/make-og-card.py calls it 'the full-size source art' and 'the source painting'. Neither phrase distinguishes a human illustration from a generated one, and that distinction is the whole point of the origin field.
